moments.selftext: Before Robert Pattinson became one of Hollywood’s biggest stars, he admitted to inventing a far more prestigious background for himself. He claimed he had studied at Oxford and trained at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, even telling people in Los Angeles that Prince William had attended RADA with him. The stories were completely fabricated. Pattinson later admitted that he assumed Americans would believe almost anything an English actor told them if it sounded prestigious enough. He also became surprisingly open in interviews about his habit of making up stories.

moments.selftext: “A crooked tree lives its own life, but a straight tree is turned into wood.” - Chinese Proverb The idea behind this proverb comes most clearly from the writings of Zhuangzi, one of the central thinkers of Daoism in the 4th century BCE. In the Zhuangzi, a famous story tells of a large, twisted tree that carpenters ignore because its wood is unsuitable for construction. Precisely because it is considered “useless,” the tree is never cut down and survives to live out its natural life. Zhuangzi uses the tree as a metaphor for human life. In Daoist thought, being “useful” by conventional standards can make a person vulnerable to exploitation, control, and exhaustion. Those who are unconventional, overlooked, or unwilling to fit society’s expectations may instead preserve their freedom and live on their own terms.
